claims.statement: runMode in src/modes.ts is the pipeline orchestrator: one entrypoint taking AppConfig, CliOptions, and a ModeCaller, dispatching to schema, multi, retrieve, deepresearch, or the single Grok call, and returning one normalized PipelineResult.

Dispatch priority is strict: --schema runs first and takes over the single-call path regardless of mode; then multi; then the retrieve branch (mode retrieve or --retrieve/--output results|both on web-capable modes); then deepresearch; then the generic single Grok call tail.

The retrieve branch is not limited to retrieve mode: --retrieve or --output results/both on any web-capable Grok mode routes to runRetrieve, while on non-web modes (deepresearch, multi) those flags are ignored with a warning.

Single-call Grok tail: auto/expert use the expert model alias, fast uses the fast alias; the call is built by buildSingleCallMessages at temperature 0.2 with json and resolved web options; deepresearch uses the deepResearch alias with buildResearchMessages.

Two-pass invariant: --json + web and --schema + web always run a tools-enabled research pass (json false) followed by a tool-less format pass (json true, messages from buildJsonFromResearchMessages or buildSchemaFromResearchMessages), because response_format json_object combined with OpenRouter server tools has been observed to collapse to garbage JSON like -1.5e-05 on Grok.
The two-pass format pass runs without web tools and does not re-inject X/bookmark markdown; it is grounded only in the research content plus source URLs.

Two-pass results are merged by concatenating sources and warnings and merging usage with mergeUsage; the --json variant appends a warning explaining the two-pass pattern was used to avoid json_object+tools failures.
--schema overrides deepresearch and multi with a warning, resolving the fast alias for fast mode and the expert alias otherwise, and takes a single schema call when web is disabled.
loadSchema treats the --schema value as inline JSON when it parses, otherwise reads it as a file path and throws if the file cannot be read.
multi runs 5 calls: 1 Sonar research call (research alias), 3 Grok role analyses (engineering, product, skeptic), and 1 Grok synthesis call; no multi leg carries web tools.

Multi analysis legs run in parallel by default (Promise.allSettled) but sequentially under --max-cost (runSequential), so the withBudget pre-check stops dispatching further billable legs the moment the cap is crossed.

Multi tolerates partial role failure by converting failed roles into warnings and proceeding to synthesis, but rethrows a MaxCostExceededError from any leg as fatal, fails the run if research fails, and throws if all three analysis roles fail.

The retrieve call uses role retrieve with buildRetrieveMessages, json true, temperature 0.1 and web attached; parseRetrieveContent plus mergeRetrieveResults build searchResults; --output both adds a synthesis call at temperature 0.2 with web intentionally off because grounding is already in the retrieved sources block.

withBudget wraps the raw caller when maxCost is set, maintains cumulative spent and a costKnown flag, performs a pre-check before each call and a post-check after adding each call's costUsd, and throws MaxCostExceededError immediately when cumulative spend exceeds the cap; the error names the role the run aborted after.
A single call that itself exceeds --max-cost is caught by the post-check; the maximum overrun exposure is one call because a call's cost is only known after it completes.

If any call's costUsd is undefined, withBudget's costKnown flips false and enforcement degrades: cli.ts prints a warning that --max-cost was set but OpenRouter returned no cost, so the limit was not enforced.

runMode gathers the X signal and bookmark search before dispatching any model call; skipping bookmark searches (missing key, rate limit, or any error) produces warnings rather than hard failures and the full BookmarkSearchResult travels on PipelineResult.bookmarks.

X markdown and formatted bookmarks are injected into prompts through withContext as framed sample context (X is not ground truth; bookmarks are prior personal context), with system-prompt instructions to include ## X signal and ## Saved bookmarks sections when material.
--schema injects the X signal into the prompt via withXInSchemaPrompt, and the retrieve --output both synthesis appends X/bookmarks blocks to its sources block.

attachContext attaches PipelineResult.xSignal and .bookmarks and folds their warnings into result.warnings; warnings are deduped across branch warnings, deprecations, signals, and parse failures by dedupeWarnings.

--x-only returns a zero-cost X Signal Brief result (emptyUsage, no sources, web off) and --bookmarks-only returns a zero-cost Saved Bookmarks Brief with sources derived from hits and related groups; combining the two flags throws Cannot combine --x-only with --bookmarks-only.

normalizeResult, normalizeRetrieveResult, and normalizeSchemaResult all stamp mode, profile, outputFormat and deduped warnings and overwrite per-call web flags using modeAllowsWeb so non-web modes always report web false/false, replacing the auto/quality/raw placeholders the OpenRouter client sets.
normalizeSchemaResult parses result.content as JSON into schemaResult when valid and omits it (with a warning) when the model returns invalid JSON, keeping the raw text in content; it drops answer.

normalizeRetrieveResult drops answer, sets searchResults, and gives content semantics per --output: results mode uses the optional LLM answer or an empty string, while both mode keeps the synthesis in content.

parseDecisionAnswer tolerates failure: non-JSON content, non-object JSON (including bare numbers like -1.5e-05), and empty garbage objects become warnings with answer omitted and content preserved; it coerces fields leniently and maps confidence to low/high only, medium otherwise, and never throws.
normalizeResult only parses DecisionAnswer for --json runs without schema, outputStyle results, retrieve flag, or retrieve mode.
Progress lines (Step 1/2, Step 2/3, Step 1/1) go to stderr and are gated on !options.json so --json stdout stays pure; multi prints Step 1/3 through Step 3/3.
Mode names with web: modeAllowsWeb returns true only for auto, fast, expert, and retrieve; retrieve mode forces web search on (unless --no-web) while fetch stays opt-in.

Under --max-cost, multi research plus the first crossing analysis leg are the only calls dispatched, and later legs plus synthesis are never sent; the worst case bills only the leg that detects the overrun.
